title: Enzyme inhibition and metabolic control; Energy and thermodynamics in living systems; ATP; Evidence for evolution; Respiration overview and glycolysis
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: BM14#t1 term and clue written for the game; BM14#t2 term and clue written for the game; BM14#t3 term and clue written for the game; EZ03#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: BM11#N.5b, BM14#N.2, EV03a#N.5b, EV03b#N.3, EZ03#N.2, RS01#N.2b, BM11#N.10b, BM14#N.13, EV03a#N.7b, EV03b#N.7b, EZ03#N.14, RS01#N.9b.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: First law of thermodynamics
items.clue: Energy is never created or destroyed, only transformed

items.label: Entropy
items.clue: Disorder: every energy transformation increases it in the universe

items.label: Coupling
items.clue: Linking an energy-releasing process such as ATP hydrolysis to an energy-requiring one

items.label: Active site
items.clue: Where the substrate normally binds; a molecule of similar shape can occupy it instead.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of an energy-releasing process coupled with an energy-requiring process in a cell?

options.text: Heat released by respiration supplying the energy to join amino acids into proteins
Mitochondria creating new energy that is then used for the contraction of muscles
ATP hydrolysis supplying the energy for O₂ to diffuse into a cell across its membrane
ATP hydrolysis supplying the energy needed to pump ions against their concentration gradient

questions.explanation: Pumping ions against their concentration gradient (active transport) requires energy. It is coupled with ATP hydrolysis, which releases energy, so the coupled process as a whole releases energy and can proceed.

questions.stem: Which statement about the energy requirements of living cells is correct?

options.text: Cells that are growing or dividing need an energy input, but resting cells need none.
Cells recycle their energy, so they need an input of energy only to start their processes.
Every living cell needs a continual input of energy, as some energy is always lost as heat.
Animal cells need an energy input, but plant cells make their own energy by photosynthesis instead.

questions.explanation: All living systems require an input of energy. Cells use energy to build molecules, move substances and maintain order, and every energy transformation releases some energy as heat, so energy must be continually supplied.

questions.stem: A biologist hypothesizes that a hypothetical rodent species, X, is more closely related to species Y than to species Z. Which investigation would best test this hypothesis?

options.text: Compare one gene's sequence in all three species, since differences build up over time.
Compare the habitats of X, Y and Z, since closely related species live in similar places.
Measure the amount of DNA in a cell of each species, since related species have equal amounts.
Compare the body sizes of X, Y and Z, since closely related species are similar in size.

questions.stem: Carbon-14 has a half-life of about 5,730 years. A paleontologist finds a fossil bone in rock layers that are about 70 million years old. Which statement about dating this fossil is correct?

options.text: It is dated by its depth in the rock, as every meter of rock took the same time to form.
Its carbon-14 decayed with a shorter half-life, because the fossil holds so little carbon.
It can be dated from the carbon-14 in the volcanic rock layers just above and below it.
Too little carbon-14 would remain, so other isotopes in nearby volcanic rock are used.

questions.stem: In a hypothetical bacterium, compound S is made from compound P by a pathway of three enzyme-catalysed steps: P → Q → R → S. Enzyme 1 converts P to Q, enzyme 2 converts Q to R, and enzyme 3 converts R to S. A mutation makes enzyme 2 non-functional. Which prediction about the mutant bacterium is best supported?

options.text: Only R is affected; Q and S are still made at their usual rates in the mutant.
Q builds up, and far less R and S are made than in bacteria that lack the mutation.
S is made at the usual rate, as the cell makes a new enzyme because it needs S.
P builds up and no Q is made, as the whole pathway stops at its first step.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes what cellular respiration does in a cell?

options.text: It transfers energy from organic molecules such as glucose to ATP, which then powers cell work.
It creates new energy from glucose and stores that energy in ATP, which then powers cell work.
It converts the matter of glucose into energy, which is stored in ATP to power cell work.
It is the exchange of O₂ and CO₂ by breathing, which supplies the cell with energy for its work.

questions.explanation: Energy already stored in organic molecules is transferred to ATP (and partly released as heat); ATP then powers cellular work.

questions.stem: The model compares the energy of the reactants and products of reaction 1, which joins molecules A and B, of reaction 2, the hydrolysis of ATP, and of the two reactions coupled together in a cell. Which statement about the coupled reaction is supported by the model?

options.text: Overall it releases energy, as reaction 2 releases more energy than reaction 1 requires.
It can proceed because breaking a bond in ATP releases energy, as breaking any bond does.
Coupling creates the extra energy that reaction 1 needs, so the total energy rises.
Reaction 1 releases the energy that drives reaction 2, the hydrolysis of ATP.

questions.stem: Burning glucose in a flame and breaking it down in a cell's respiration pathway release the same total energy. Which statement best explains why cells use a pathway of many enzyme-catalyzed steps?

options.text: Many small steps release more energy in total than a single step does, so the cell gains extra energy.
Each step runs on its own, so if one enzyme is blocked the steps before and after carry on as usual.
In small steps, part of the energy can be captured in ATP instead of all being released at once as heat.
The enzyme at each step supplies some energy to its reaction, so the pathway needs less energy from glucose.

questions.stem: Biologists discover a single-celled organism whose cells contain a nucleus, mitochondria and an endoplasmic reticulum, each enclosed by membranes. Which conclusion is best supported?

options.text: It is the ancestor from which fungi, plants and animals all evolved.
It will in time become a multicellular organism, since it is still primitive.
It is a bacterium, since bacteria are the organisms that are made of a single cell.
It shares an ancestor with fungi, plants and animals that had these organelles.

questions.explanation: Membrane-bound organelles are shared by eukaryotes and indicate their common ancestry.

questions.stem: Breeders of a dog breed mate only dogs that closely match a strict breed standard, and they often mate close relatives. Compared with a large population of mixed-breed dogs, which outcome is expected for the breed?

options.text: Less genetic variation, because only dogs with a narrow set of traits pass on their alleles
More genetic variation, because breeders keep selecting for new traits in each generation
The same genetic variation, because breeding changes how dogs look but not their genes
Fewer inherited disorders, because breeders mate the healthiest and best dogs with each other

questions.stem: Methanol is not very toxic itself, but the enzyme alcohol dehydrogenase converts it into toxic products. Ethanol is also a substrate of alcohol dehydrogenase. Doctors have treated methanol poisoning by giving ethanol. Why does this reduce the harm?

options.text: Ethanol binds to an allosteric site, so the active site changes shape and methanol cannot bind.
Ethanol denatures alcohol dehydrogenase, so no methanol at all is converted.
Ethanol competes with methanol for the active site, so less methanol is converted at a time.
Ethanol binds to methanol molecules, so less methanol is free to reach the enzyme.
Glucose is oxidized by O₂ to pyruvate, forming ATP from ADP and releasing CO₂ and H₂O as well.
Glucose is broken down to pyruvate, forming ATP from ADP and NADH from NAD⁺; no O₂ is used.
Glucose is split into pyruvate and NADH, and all of the ATP is made later, in the mitochondria.
Glucose is converted to lactic acid and ATP, and this happens only when no O₂ is present in the cell.

questions.explanation: Glycolysis releases energy in glucose to form ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate, NADH from NAD⁺, and pyruvate, without O₂.
